prompt_en: Create a photorealistic editorial photograph set in a temporary bookbinding studio inside a decommissioned mountaintop cable-car signal cabin during a sleet storm. An unmistakably adult woman sits at a scarred workbench; her visible adult face, hair length, hair color, hair texture, hair part, general complexion, and facial features follow the supplied appearance reference. She hand-sews a palm-sized accordion weather diary: her left hand pins the folded indigo paper signatures against a wooden sewing cradle while her right hand pulls waxed crimson linen thread through a punched sewing station, leaving a clearly visible tightening stitch. Frame a medium-wide eye-level environmental portrait so her face, both hands, the sewing cradle, the practical, and the window remain legible in one frame; use a natural 35mm perspective with enough depth for the lamp-to-subject-to-window relation. A lit green-shaded brass desk lamp is visibly present beside the tools; at least one plausible practical source is visible within the scene. A nearby brightness and color pool falls off outward from that source. Light reaching the subject matches the practical's plausible direction and color family. A second ambient zone remains spatially distinct in color brightness or direction: cold overcast storm light through wet glass stays blue-gray beside the lamp's warm pool. Cast and form shadows have coherent source ownership without teal-orange grade substitution. Through the cabin's broad window, diagonal sleet and cloud-swallowed cable towers are plainly visible. Include a bone folder, awl, thread spool, damp gloves, obsolete cable gauges, and a small brass barometer as believable working evidence. Emphasize precise hand-to-tool contact, a readable craft sequence, tactile paper fibers, wet glass, and grounded photographic realism.
negative_en: over-processed retouching, unrealistic hands, broken facial features, illustration look, 3D render look, low resolution, plastic-looking skin, distorted fingers
